title: IBM research exposes the consistency gap hidden by average agent scores
friendlyTitle: An AI agent that succeeds once may fail the same task next time
summary: IBM researchers report that a GPT-4.1 ReAct agent averaged 77.4% success across repeated AppWorld runs but completed every one of five attempts for only 53% of tasks. Their Consistency Analyzer identifies decisions likely to change between runs, while generated guidelines reduced the reported consistency gap from 24.4 to 12 percentage points.
friendlySummary: IBM found a large gap between an agent’s average score and the number of tasks it completed correctly every time. Its new tool looks for decision points where the agent may change course.
whyItMatters: An average benchmark can hide whether a workflow behaves dependably for one user doing the same job twice. Teams should add repeated-run measures to agent evaluation and examine unstable tool choices before assigning high-consequence work.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Reliable work needs more than one successful demo. Test the same task several times and study where the agent makes different choices.
